points.quote: Your assessments will fall into one of the following three categories. Each assessment brief will state clearly which one of the categories applies.
points.anchor: Can I use AI in assessments?
points.gist: Assessments fall into one of three categories, and each assessment brief states which one applies.

points.quote: You must always check your assessment brief for the requirements of your module and if you have any doubts as to the extent to which genAI use may be allowed in an assessment, please always speak to the module leader.
points.anchor: Can I use AI in assessments?
points.gist: Always check your assessment brief, and if in doubt about how far genAI use is allowed, speak to the module leader.

points.quote: Neither a proof-reader nor a proof-reading tool (whether genAI or not) can ever be used to make changes to your work directly; the proof-reader or proof reading tool must only identify potential changes which you must then choose to accept or reject; this will ensure that you remain the author of your work.
points.gist: A proof-reader or proof-reading tool, genAI or not, can never change your work directly; it may only identify changes that you accept or reject.
A proofreader or genAI tool may identify areas for possible improvement.

points.quote: Restrictions on AI will also apply to proofreading.
points.gist: Restrictions on AI also apply to proofreading.

points.quote: If you use AI in an assessment, you must disclose your use in line with the requirements of your assessment brief.
points.anchor: Do I need to declare AI use?
points.gist: If you use AI in an assessment, you must disclose it in line with your assessment brief's requirements.

points.quote: For your privacy, security and academic integrity, we recommend using University-supported AI tools rather than external alternatives.
points.gist: For privacy, security and academic integrity, University-supported AI tools are recommended over external alternatives.

points.quote: Gemini Notebook – an AI-powered study and research tool that helps you understand, organise and summarise information from your own study materials.
points.anchor: Which AI tools can I use at Herts?
points.gist: Gemini Notebook is an AI study and research tool that helps understand, organise and summarise information from your own study materials.

points.quote: When using these tools for your studies, sign in with your University account.
points.gist: When using these tools for your studies, sign in with your University account.

points.quote: The University's position on AI, proofreading, academic integrity and academic misconduct is outlined in the Academic Integrity and Academic Misconduct Policy (UPR AS14 Appendix III).
points.anchor: Can I use AI in assessments?
points.gist: The University's position on AI, proofreading, integrity and misconduct is in the Academic Integrity and Academic Misconduct Policy (UPR AS14 Appendix III).
